title: Marisa
subtitle: Static dictionaries with fast prefix lookup.
intro: Build a compact MARISA trie from a column of strings. Store the trie as a BLOB and use it for exact membership, autocomplete, or prefix-rule matching.

reference.name: marisa_trie(text)
reference.description: Aggregate a column of strings into one trie BLOB.

reference.name: marisa_predictive(trie, prefix, limit)
reference.description: Return stored strings that begin with the supplied prefix.

reference.name: marisa_common_prefix(trie, text, limit)
reference.description: Return stored strings that are prefixes of the supplied text.

notes.title: Two directions of prefix search
notes.body: Predictive search expands a short input into longer dictionary entries. Common-prefix search finds shorter stored rules matching the start of a longer input.

notes.title: Build for a static set
notes.body: Rebuild the aggregate when the dictionary changes. Normalize case and whitespace before both construction and querying if those differences should be ignored.

examples.title: Build a dictionary
examples.sql:
CREATE TABLE dictionary AS
SELECT marisa_trie(name) AS trie
FROM (VALUES ('Alice'), ('Megan'),
             ('Melissa')) AS t(name);
examples.caption: One result row stores the entire dictionary.

examples.title: Lookup & autocomplete
examples.sql:
SELECT marisa_lookup(trie, 'Alice') AS found,
       marisa_predictive(trie, 'Me', 10)
         AS suggestions
FROM dictionary;
examples.caption: found is true; suggestions includes Megan and Melissa.

examples.title: Match stored prefixes
examples.caption: The matching rules are U, US and USA; the limit caps the result count.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT marisa_lookup(trie,'Alice') AND NOT marisa_lookup(trie,'Unknown') AND len(marisa_predictive(trie,'Me',10))=2 FROM dictionary) THEN true ELSE error('trie lookup') END;
